children: Palisade Bio reported a third-quarter 2026 net loss of $14.6 million, or $0.07 per share, compared with a $2.9 million loss a year earlier. The company ended September with $113.6 million in cash and cash equivalents. It also reported progress in its Phase 2 programs for PALI-2108, including dosing the first patient in its ulcerative colitis trial.
Third-quarter license revenue was $0; revenue for the first nine months of 2026 was $500,000, compared with none in the same 2025 period.
Research and development expenses were $10.6 million in the quarter, up from $1.4 million a year earlier.
General and administrative expenses were $5.1 million, compared with $1.5 million in the third quarter of 2025.
Loss from operations was $15.7 million; net loss was $14.6 million, or $0.07 per basic and diluted share. The year-earlier quarter’s net loss was $2.9 million, or $0.38 per share.

Cash and cash equivalents totaled $113.6 million as of September 30, 2026. Palisade Bio expects its cash to fund operations through the anticipated primary efficacy readouts for ASCENTRA-UC and ASCENTRA-CD.

Palisade Bio dosed the first patient in the global Phase 2b ASCENTRA-UC trial on October 27. The study is expected to enroll about 204 patients and compare once-daily 15 mg and 30 mg doses of PALI-2108 with placebo; topline induction results are expected in Q4 2027.

The company activated 29 of 30 planned U.S. trial sites and is expanding ASCENTRA-UC toward approximately 115 sites globally. It received Health Canada clearance in September and regulatory clearance in the Republic of Georgia in October, with other submissions under review.

The FDA cleared the PALI-2108 IND for Crohn’s disease, enabling the Phase 2a ASCENTRA-CD study. The open-label study is expected to enroll about 60 adults, with enrollment targeted for Q1 2027 and the primary efficacy readout expected in Q1 2028.

Palisade Bio presented five posters at ACG 2026, including two selected for Presidential Poster Awards, and additional findings at UEG Week 2026. These included exploratory data reporting endoscopic improvement within two weeks in a five-patient cohort with fibrostenotic Crohn’s disease.
